146.t: Violence at White dances: Marlow and West Texas cowboys
146.s: Booking agents sat at the door; a man attacked musicians in Marlow, cowboys demanded they keep playing, and Smith says they put it down to ignorance.
146.ch: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
146.q: ...sit right on the floor where the people were dancing. I remember, we was in Marlow, Oklahoma, a little town out there in the western part of Oklahoma, and we was playing a White dance. A little old fellow came by dancing with his girlfriend...with a lady; I guess it might have been his wife. But…

146.t: The sheriff who wanted only Turkey in the Straw
146.s: At Palestine, Texas, a sheriff with two pistols danced alone while the band played Turkey in the Straw all night.
146.ch: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
146.q: Yeah, yeah. Not only that, we ran into... There was a dance down here in Palestina... See, we knew how to handle all the (?)s... We still didn't think about that. We watched out for that. And we ...(?). . .(?). . . down there at Palestina.

146.t: Snub Mosely's story and the bottle thrown at Cab Calloway
146.s: Asked about violence, Smith tells of a bottle meant for Cab Calloway that hit a drummer later in Don Redman's band.
146.ch: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
146.q: Yeah. I knew Snub. He was in the last band I played with, up in New York. Cab was down there in St. Petersburg, and we had a drummer down there with us in Don Redman's band that had got hit.

259.t: Amos White, and a Creole jazz band job that ended in a brawl
259.s: Vincent talks about Amos White, then tells of his Creole jazz band playing a rough job where drunken patrons turned on them, and the band left with about $35 each.
259.q: He wasn't from here. I didn't forget where he was. But he'd come down there and stay at Goodwire. He was a learning type of printing. And Lewis used to come around us all the time. He was a professor. You know, he was a musician. And we played with him. I had the Marlene Creole jazz band. That's…

302.s: On the morning before the accident, a drunk white man with a pistol made him dance, then gave him a drink and a dollar.
302.q: That same morning when I was pulling out, there's a little grocery store that was next to the lot where we were parked. We had a bus where the couples stayed. There was, let's see, one, two, three, four, five, six, eight couples that stayed on this bus. They opened the bus up and made compartments…

58.s: Punch recounts a show MC beating a white drunk and getting away.

144.t: Held at gunpoint by a New Jersey state trooper; Billie's words
144.s: Fuller recounts a trooper throwing his trombone off the Turnpike bridge, and Billie Holiday telling him he would always make it.
144.q: I’ve always felt that in some way, and I don’t know how, that I was covered and I was going to make it. I’ve been in situations that are unbelievable. I don’t drive a car now because I had this new car; I was in New York. I bought an old something with the white colored roof. I was coming from a…

67.t: Corn whiskey and thrown bottles in Miami
67.s: At a whites-only Miami venue hecklers made him drink corn whiskey, then bottles hit the drummer.
67.ch: Cab Calloway on the road and segregation
67.q: playing there at a big place there, it was a white place, did not allowed colored in it. So a couple of guys standing out in the front heckling the band, you know, and they -- one called me, and I went over there cause I was a Southerner and I don't have problems with the Southerners. This guy had…

231.t: Racist men at the door and the fight
231.s: Men tipped off by a dancer came knocking, called the girls nigger lovers and hit one; Bubbles grabbed a man and tripped his helper.
231.ch: Solo years, marriages and the Canadian party
231.q: Now this boy was a dancer, he was the guy -- he didn't think much of negroes in the first place. He made you think he did, but he don't. Anyway he got the fellas in the lobby to tell them about the party going on and about Buck and I being there. So a couple of the guys, and they may have had a…

383.t: The Dallas centennial incident and the police chief
383.s: A professor sends champagne backstage, a policeman throws him out, and the Dallas police chief tells Wilson and Hampton he would protect them.
383.ch: Later career and The Benny Goodman Story
383.q: We had one incident in Dallas, Texas, very interesting. At the centennial down there, about 1937, I guess, and there was some ruckus backstage. A friend of mine, one of the professors from the University of Texas, had a few drinks and then sent some champagne backstage to Lionel and me. And he not…

74.t: A racist radio introduction and Crooke faces down a bully
74.s: At WFAA opening night the announcer introduces them with a slur; the next day Crooke subdues a would-be tough with his revolver.
74.ch: Trent's band: touring, sidemen and breakup
74.q: We were broadcasting, and the announcer was the owner and opening night he said, ladies and gentlemen, I want you to hear the greatest nigger band you ever heard in your life, and we all turned around and looked, what is this; just give me one more minute to tell you about these niggers. 455.s: After the flag-waver a drunk insults Hines, who answers sharply, while Budd unlatches his brother's pistol in the briefcase.
455.ch: Hines 1935-38, Gus Arnheim and Billy Eckstine
455.q: So we played. We used to play five numbers to a set. So on the ending of our set we played what we called the flag waver.
